 (b) (1) The legislative body of a local agency may adopt reasonable regulations to ensure
 that the intent of the subdivision (a) is carried out, including, but not limited to, regulations
 limiting the total amount of time allocated for public testimony on particular issues and for
 each individual speaker.
  (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), when the legislative body of a local agency limits
 time for public comment, the legislative body of a local agency shall provide at least twice
 the allotted time to a member of the public who utilizes a translator to ensure that non-
 English speakers receive the same opportunity to directly address the legislative body of
 a local agency.”

 In furtherance of Section 54954.3 of the Brown Act, the public is allotted to speak a total
 of two (2) minutes on the entirety of the Consent Calendar, Appointment(s), New
 Business and Closed Session, with two (2) minutes on each Public Hearing, and, if
 desired, an additional two (2) minutes on items not on the agenda that are within the
 subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council. As specified in the Brown Act, a speaker
 utilizing a translator will receive twice the amount of time specified.

SUBJECT:  RECEIVE AND FILE THE MONTHLY INVESTMENT ACTIVITY
  REPORT FOR JANUARY 2024

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the monthly investment activity
reports for the City of Palmdale and Successor Agency for January 2024.

BACKGROUND

Pursuant to Section 16 of the City and Successor Agency Investment Policy, the City
Treasurer shall prepare and present monthly and quarterly reports on investments to
the City Manager/Executive Director and the City Council/Directors. The reports shall
detail the type of investment, name of the issuer, purchase date, date of maturity,
amount of deposit, and rate of interest. This information shall be provided for all City and
Successor Agency pooled investments, as well as for Certificates of Participation,
Revenue Bonds, Tax Allocation Bonds, Assessment Districts, and Community Facilities
District accounts, which are managed by outside Fiscal Agents.

The monthly investment reports provide a synopsis of the investment activity for the City
and Successor Agency. The reports provide information on assets, allocations, average
maturities, yields, and book valuations. The interest rates presented are the most current
rates available as of the date of this report.

The market values presented for pooled City and Successor Agency investments are
based on closing prices for the related investment as of the date of this report. This
information was obtained from the Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg Financial Markets,
Capital Market Finances, or other reliable sources of market prices.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Monthly Investment Reports
March 6, 2024
Page 2

DISCUSSION

Compliance with Investment Policy

For January, the invested portfolio amount for the City totaled $322,768,158, an
increase of $16,363,019 from the previous month and an increase of $20,693,983
compared to last year. The monthly increase results from U.S. Treasury investments
purchased during the month, in addition to interest earnings.

The par value of Successor Agency’s portfolio as of January was $13,321,192. The
balance increased by $6,344,627 from last month due to Los Angeles County property
taxes received during the month.

All investments meet criteria appropriate to Section 8 of the Investment Policy. The
portfolios are based on a combination of various investments, including CDs, Corporate
Notes, U.S. Treasury Securities, and Government Agency Paper, each adhering to
portfolio percentage limitations.

The Finance Division is the custodian for the City and Successor Agency’s investment
portfolio and follows the three main principles of both entities’ investment policies 1)
Investment in financial instruments that mitigate the risk of monetary losses stemming
from market fluctuations; 2) Establish and maintain a portfolio that has sufficient liquidity
to allow the City and Successor Agency to meet all anticipated cash requirements; and
3) Seek out investment instruments that provide a competitive market rate of return.

Liquidity

One core approach the Finance Division focuses on is providing liquidity to measure up
to the City and Successor Agency’s operational requirements. Thus, the Finance
Division is currently investing in two pooled funds, Local Agency Investment Fund (LAIF)
and California Asset Management Program (CAMP). These are intended for daily
operational activities and used for economic uncertainties and maintenance needs. The
pooled funds provide a higher liquidity ratio to ensure the City and Successor Agency
meet cash flow requirements.

The total LAIF balance for the City at the end of January is $130,013,401. An increase
of $1,309,470 from the prior month due to interest gains.

Successor Agency LAIF balance at the end of January was $6,283,347. An increase of
$67,515 from the prior month due to interest gains.

CAMP’s balance for the City at the end of January was $15,288,256 compared to
December balance of $266,599. The increase is due to a transfer made to CAMP from
General bank, and interest earned during the month.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Monthly Investment Reports
March 6, 2024
Page 3

The interest rates presented are the most current rates available as of the date of this
report. As of January 31, 2024, the interest rates for LAIF and CAMP investments were
at 4.012 percent and 5.54 percent, respectively. By comparison, the LAIF and CAMP
interest rates at the end of December were 3.929 percent and 5.55 percent. This time
last year, LAIF and CAMP rates were at 2.425 percent and 4.53, respectively.

The chart above shows the Local Agency Investment Fund and California Asset
Management Program’s average monthly yields beginning April 2023 through January
2024. The difference between the performance of the two funds is partly due to the
varying pool characteristics. CAMP’s portfolio composition is more prone to market
volatility, resulting in performance variations.

Diversity

The Finance Division aims to diversify the investment portfolios to avoid incurring
unreasonable and avoidable risks regarding specific security types or individual financial
institutions.

The City and Successor Agency’s investment portfolios remain strongly diversified. The
monthly and quarterly report includes all investments held by both entities and current
book values as of January 31, 2024.

The City and Successor Agency is expected to have sufficient sums of money to meet
their expenditure requirements for the next six months. The Finance Division will
continue to monitor current economic conditions and the impact on interest rates.

Attached are summaries of the investments in the City and Successor Agency’s books
as of January 31, 2024.

FISCAL IMPACT

There is no fiscal impact associated with the recommended actions for this report.

STRATEGIC PLAN

  B. Manage resources, costs, and liabilities to ensure the City’s long-term fiscal
  health.

  C. Involve and expand engagement to enhance public oversight and
  transparency.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2024-020, a Resolution of the City Council adopting the
  Joint Resolution of the Board of Supervisors of the County of Los Angeles, acting
  on behalf of the Los Angeles County General Fund and the Los Angeles County
  Consolidated Fire Protection District, the Board of Directors of County Sanitation
  District No. 20 of Los Angeles County, and the Governing Bodies of the Antelope
  Valley Cemetery District, the Antelope Valley Mosquito and Vector Control
  District, the City of Palmdale, and the Palmdale Water District - Zone E, approving
  and accepting the negotiated exchange of property tax revenues resulting from
  the annexation of property designated as Annexation 20-104 with the County
  Sanitation District No. 20 of Los Angeles County; and,
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Resolution No. CC 2024-020
March 6, 2024
Page 2

  2. Authorize the Mayor to execute the Joint Tax Sharing Resolution No. CC 2024-
  020, approving and accepting the negotiated exchange of property tax revenues
  resulting from the annexation of property designated as Annexation 20-104 with
  the County Sanitation District No. 20 of Los Angeles County; and

  3. Authorize the Mayor to execute the County Sanitation District No. 20 of Los
  Angeles Joint Resolution, approving and accepting the Negotiated Exchange of
  property tax revenues resulting from the annexation of property designated as
  Annexation 20-104 with the County Sanitation District No. 20 of Los Angeles
  County.

BACKGROUND

In accordance with the Revenue and Tax Code (Sections 99 and 99.01), any time there
is a jurisdictional change that results in a special district providing a new service not
previously provided to an area, the law requires the governing bodies of all local
agencies that receive a portion of that property tax determined by resolution the amount
of the annual tax increase to be transferred to that special district. The existing tax
revenue based on the property’s assessed value received by agencies will not change.
Based on the increased property valuation assessment, this resolution only affects a
percentage of future revenue agencies would receive.

DISCUSSION

In the attached Los Angeles County Sanitation District letter dated October 23, 2023,

revenue based on the property’s assessed value received by agencies will not change.
Based on the increased property valuation assessment, this resolution only affects a

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement No. A-8602 with Parkwood Landscape Maintenance, Inc., in
  an amount not to exceed $16,120,000 for the remaining three months of fiscal year
  2023-2024 and the subsequent four fiscal years for a total contract term of 51
  months; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8602
  with Parkwood Landscape Maintenance, Inc., including minimal and/or non-
  substantive changes.

BACKGROUND

The City administers service agreements with contractors specializing in various
professional disciplines to assist with department operations; this includes landscape
maintenance services for 238 Landscape Assessment Districts (5,565,318 square feet)
and 58 General Benefit areas (1,737,013 square feet) citywide.

Over the last twenty years, the City has contracted these services in some capacity to
meet the increasing maintenance requirements and community expectations. During the
previous solicitation for these services, the City Council directed staff to address
enhanced oversight and contract compliance verification. Therefore, these components
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Approve Landscape Maintenance Services Agreement, Agreement No. A-8602
March 6, 2024
Page 2

were built into the resulting agreement and ensured contractor accountability for the
maintenance services provided.

For this solicitation and agreement, staff expanded upon the scope of work and technical
specifications and enhanced the contract measures, incorporating compliance-based
penalties and liquidated damages. This will ensure the contractor meets requirements
and provides quality landscape maintenance services to the City.

Landscape maintenance services include, but are not limited to, the following:
   Turf mowing, edging, detailing, de-thatching, and aeration
   Pruning and rejuvenation of shrubs and ground cover plants
   Litter control, including disposal of trash and debris at City disposal sites
   Repairing irrigation mainlines, valves, lateral lines, and sprinklers
   Broadleaf weed control in medians, planters, niches, and adjacent right of ways up
  to the edge of pavement
   Fertilization of turf, shrubs, ground cover, and trees
   Hardscape cleaning
   Tree maintenance, including pruning, staking, tying, and guying of trees
   Cleaning flowlines and gutters, where applicable

These services provided by the landscape contractor, in conjunction with work performed
by City staff, will meet increased service demands, address routine and deferred
maintenance, and further the efficiency of operations to maintain safe, clean, and
attractive public spaces and infrastructure for the community.

DISCUSSION

The City released Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 23-001-3610 for Landscape
Maintenance Services on September 28, 2023. Notification of the RFP release was sent
electronically to registered vendors on PlanetBids, with 19 vendors registered as prime
contractors. The solicitation was also published in the Antelope Valley Press.

A mandatory pre-bid meeting was held on October 11, 2023, with seven prospective
bidders attending. The pre-bid meeting offered prospective bidders a review of the
solicitation requirements and accountability measures to be enforced and afforded an
opportunity to ask other questions regarding the bid.

Professional Landscape Maintenance Services in Landscape Assessment Districts
(LADs), General Benefit Landscape Areas (GBA), and Fairway Business Park (FBP).

SECTION A. INTENT OF SPECIFICATIONS
The Contractor agrees to provide services according to the highest quality landscape industry
accepted standards, employing up-to-date methods, procedures, and controls for landscape
maintenance consistent with the City’s landscape maintenance specifications This shall include
the use of proper knowledge, skills, materials, and equipment of a timely basis to maintain all
areas in a clean, safe, healthy, and aesthetically acceptable manner during the entire term of this
contract.

 SECTION B. GENERAL MAINTENANCE SPECIFICATIONS
General Maintenance Specifications are applicable to all landscape areas serviced under this
Agreement, including Landscape Assessment Districts, General Benefit Landscape Areas, and
Fairway Business Park.
The CITY will accept NO less than full completion of the following functions during applicable
weekly or biweekly service days and within the full span of each landscape service area. Failure
to comply with this expectation will result in compliance-based punitive penalties and/or liquidated
damages as defined in Section L.
B.1  Service Frequency
Services for all locations within the designated landscape areas under this Agreement shall be
performed at the following frequency, unless otherwise noted.
Landscape Assessment Districts
Services in all Landscape Assessment District locations shall be performed one time per week
(weekly), unless otherwise noted.
General Benefit Landscape Areas and Fairway Business Park
Services in all General Benefit Landscape areas and Fairway Business Park shall be performed
once every two weeks (biweekly), unless otherwise noted.

 Landscape Areas  Service Frequency
 Landscape Assessment Districts  Weekly
 General Benefit Landscape Areas and Fairway Business Park  Bi-weekly

B.2  Drains and Grates
Drainage infrastructure including channels and gutters within maintained landscape areas and up
to the edge of asphalt pavement shall be kept free of vegetation, debris, and algae to allow the
unrestricted flow of water. Plugged drains, and missing or damaged grates shall be reported to
the superintendent or appointed designee immediately.
B.3  Reporting of Landscape Pests and Disease
During regularly scheduled maintenance, the CONTRACTOR shall inspect all areas being
serviced for the presence of disease, insect and/or rodent infestation. The CONTRACTOR shall
immediately notify the superintendent or appointed designee if any disease, insect and/or rodent
infestation is found.
B.4  Reporting of Plant Material Loss or Damage
The CONTRACTOR shall immediately notify the superintendent or appointed designee of any
damage and/or loss of plant material due to any cause in the serviced landscaped areas.

B.5  General Reporting Requirements
CONTRACTOR shall report the following items to the superintendent or appointed designee if
discovered in the serviced landscaped area:
  • IMMEDIATELY:  Large Roadway Debris; General Vandalism
  • DAILY:  Large Dumped Debris; Stray Shopping Carts, Graffiti
B.6  Landscape Replacement Responsibility
The CONTRACTOR shall be responsible for replacement of turf, annual plants, trees, shrubs,
ground cover when damage and/or loss is deemed to result from CONTRACTOR’s negligence of
landscape maintenance operations as specified herein. The size and species of replacement
plant material will be according to the surrounding landscape and as directed by the
superintendent or appointed designee.

SECTION C. TURF MAINTENANCE SPECIFICATIONS [TURF & MEADOW TYPE GRASS]
All specifications listed previously, and the following specifications shall apply to all serviced
landscape areas.
City will accept NO less than full completion of the following functions defined herein during
applicable service day and within the full span of each Landscape Assessment District, General
Benefit Landscape area, and Fairway Business Park. Failure to comply with this expectation will
result in a compliance based punitive penalty and/or liquidated damages.

C.1  Turf Mowing
Turf shall be mowed with power mowers. The mowers shall be maintained to provide a smooth
even cut without tearing. The reel or blade adjustment will provide a uniform, level cut without
ridges or depressions. Cutting heights for all turf shall be 2.5” or as directed by superintendent or
appointed designee.
Prior to initiating a mowing operation, the site is to be inspected by a trained and responsible
employee, who will determine the appropriate operation. Trash shall be removed so as not to be
shredded by mowers, glass bottles are not to be driven over and broken, and excessively wet turf
areas are not to be driven across. Damaged sprinkler heads and valve box covers are to be
immediately reported. Recycling mowers are required.
When mowing operations cannot be thoroughly completed within the designated time frame, the
superintendent or appointed designee shall be immediately notified through the Contractor’s
communication network.
Frequency
Mowing will occur weekly and/or bi-weekly per the respective service area during the growing
season. Mowing shall be performed at such intervals of time so that no more than one-third of the
grass blade is removed during each mowing in returning the grass to the accepted height for the
species of grass being mowed, but at intervals of no less than described in the frequency
schedule. Work shall be performed on the same day each week.
Estimated mowing per year: 33.

  EXHIBIT B  8-24
 Inclement weather may prohibit adherence to the scheduled frequency. The superintendent or
appointed designee shall reassign CONTRACTOR maintenance crews to assist city staff with
basin maintenance during inclement weather. All maintenance missed due to inclement weather
shall be rescheduled during the next scheduled frequency. Compliance based punitive penalties
will be waived during inclement weather reassignment.
C.2  Meadow Grass/Slope Maintenance
Meadow grass shall be trimmed using power trimmers to provide a smooth cut that is
approximately 10-12 inches in height. Maintenance trimming should not cut the crown of the
grass.
Frequency
Slope trimming shall be performed approximately every 4 weeks, at such intervals of time as to
maintain the grass at a height acceptable to the City, but at intervals of no less than described in
the frequency schedule. Inclement weather may preclude adherence to the frequency schedule.
The CONTRACTOR may request alteration of this trimming frequency from the superintendent or
appointed designees for reasons of rain or prolonged cold. All trimming missed due to inclement
weather shall be rescheduled and completed within three (3) working days. Failure to comply with
this expectation will result in compliance based punitive penalty.
Estimated slope trimming frequencies per year: 12.
C.3  Edging
All grass borders shall be neatly and uniformly edged or trimmed concurrent with every trimming
and/or mowing.
Turf borders along sidewalks and mow strips shall be cut with a vertical blade edger. Use of string
trimmers to perform this task is not acceptable.
Trimming around turf appurtenances (e.g., valve and meter boxes, controller enclosures, manhole
covers etc.) may be accomplished using string trimmers.
C.4  Medians/Sidewalks
Medians, hardscapes, and sidewalks shall be maintained in a weed free condition by utilizing a
selective herbicide application. This includes weeds in all paved and/or unpaved surfaces and in
joints, cracks, or other crevices within or adjoining to the curb and gutter areas, up to the edge of
asphalt pavement, within the boundaries of adjacent service area.
C.5  Turf Weeding
CONTRACTOR will supply equipment and labor at a cost in accordance with the applicable
broadleaf herbicide for weed control bid in the Additional Services Fee Schedule Exhibit to
mitigate broadleaf weeds in turf as directed by superintendent or appointed designee.
The city will purchase, and supply turf broadleaf weed control herbicides.
C.6  Clipping Pick-Up
Excessive clippings and/or debris left behind by recycling mowers shall be collected and removed
from the site prior to the completion of that day’s mowing operations or the end of the day,
whichever occurs first.
C.7  Litter and Debris Removal
Dumped debris, glass, leaves, paper, and/or other debris shall be removed and disposed of offsite
prior to mowing or trimming.
C.8  Removal of Season Leaf Litter
Accumulation of leaf and needle litter shall be removed from all landscaped areas including beds,
planters and turf areas under trees and placed in appropriate green waste trash bin(s).

  EXHIBIT B  9-24
 C.9  Clean Up
All walkways, trails, curb, and gutter shall be cleaned, and all debris disposed of offsite prior to
the completion of that day’s mowing or trimming operations. All debris generated from
CONTRACTOR’s operations shall be picked up and disposed of offsite. No debris shall be blown
into streets, roadways, or adjacent properties.

City will accept NO less than full completion of the following functions defined herein during

G.2  Pruning

  EXHIBIT B  16-24
 Most routine pruning to remove weak, diseased, or dead limbs can be accomplished at any time
during the year with little effect on the tree. As a rule, growth is maximized, and wound closure is
fastest if pruning takes place before the spring growth flush. Some trees, such as maples and
birches, tend to “bleed” if pruned early in the spring. It may be unsightly, but it is of little
consequence to the tree.
A few tree diseases, such as oak wilt, can be spread when pruning wounds allow spores access
into the tree. Susceptible trees should not be pruned during active transmission periods.
Heavy pruning just after the spring growth flush should be avoided. At that time, trees expended
a great deal of energy to produce foliage and early shoot growth. Removal of a substantial
percentage of foliage at this time can stress the tree. The “When to prune” section contains
consumer information provided by the International Society of Arboriculture.
G.3  Making Proper Pruning Cuts
Pruning cuts should be made just outside the branch collar. The branch collar contains trunk or
parent branch tissue and should not be damaged or removed. If the trunk collar has grown out on
a dead limb to be removed, make the cut just beyond the collar. Do not cut the collar.

If a large limb is to be removed, its weight should first be reduced. Making an undercut about 12
to 18 inches from the limb’s point of attachment accomplishes this. Make a second cut from the
top, directly above or a few inches farther out on the limb. Doing so removes the limb, leaving the
12- to 18-inch stub. Remove the stub by cutting back to the branch collar. This technique reduces
the possibility of tearing the bark. Tree pruning shall be performed based on the following
categories with the intent of developing structurally sound trees symmetrical in appearance with
the proper vertical and horizontal clearance. All pruning and trimming operations shall be in
accordance with ISA Standards.
  a) All suckers and sprouts shall be cut just outside the attachment collar to the trunk or limbs.
  b) All structural weaknesses such as a split crotch or limbs, or severe damage shall be
  reported to the superintendent or appointed designee.
  c) All trimmings and debris shall be removed and disposed of offsite at the end of each day’s
  work.
  d) Under no circumstances will stripping of lower branches be permitted in trees of 8” DBH
  or less. Lower branches shall be retained in a “tipped back” or pinched condition. Upon
  approval of the superintendent or appointed designee, skirting of lower branches may be
  done to mitigate irrigation coverage issues.
G.4  Staking and Tying

will be sustained by the City and that it is or will be impractical to determine the actual amount of

will pay to the City the sum of twenty-five hundred dollars ($2,500) for each working day delay in
completing the schedule set by the Contractor, as set forth in the Agreement beyond any timeline
or due date, or authorized extension. These damages shall be deducted from any monies due, or
which may thereafter become due, to the successful Contractor under the Agreement or may be
recovered by the City through any lawful means. The successful Contractor will be granted an

 extension of time and will not be assessed liquidated damages for any portion of the delay in
performance which would be excused pursuant to the force majeure provisions of the Agreement,
provided that the successful Contractor shall notify the City’s representative in writing of the
causes of delay within one (1) business day from the beginning of any such delay. The successful
Contractor shall bear the burden of proof to establish that any delay is subject to the force majeure
provisions of the Agreement.

L.4  FORCE MAJEURE
The time period(s) specified for performance of the services rendered pursuant to this Agreement
shall be extended because of any delays due to unforeseeable causes beyond the control and
without the fault or negligence of the Contractor, including, but not restricted to, acts of God or of
the public enemy, unusually severe weather (to be determined by City staff), fires, earthquakes,
floods, epidemics, quarantine restrictions, riots strikes, freight embargoes, wars, litigation, and/or
acts of any governmental agency, including the City, if the Contractor will within ten (10) days of
the commencement of such delay notify the City in writing of the causes of the delay.
The City will ascertain the facts and the extent of the delay and extend the time for performing the
services for the period of the enforced delay when and if the judgment of the superintendent, or
designee, the delay is justified. The superintendent or his designee’s, decision shall be final and
conclusive upon the parties to this Agreement. In no event shall Contractor be entitled to recover
damages against the City for any delay in the performance of this Agreement, however, caused;
Contractor’s sole remedy being extension of the Agreement pursuant to this Section.

L.5  RESTITUTION FOR PUBLIC OR PRIVATE PROPERTY DAMAGE
Any private or public property removed or damaged due to negligence or substandard
maintenance shall be replaced and or repaired at the CONTRACTOR’S expense to the absolute
satisfaction of the superintendent and/or private property owner. Replacement and or repairs shall
take place no later than five (5) working days from the date of damage, unless otherwise
authorized.

The City of Palmdale is seeking proposals from qualified and experienced firms to provide Landscape
Maintenance Services for Landscape Assessment Districts, General Benefit Landscape Areas, and Fairway

contain errors may be rejected. Conditional proposals will not be considered.

City of Palmdale Background
The City of Palmdale (City) is a charter city incorporated in 1962 that is governed by a five-member council
whose members are elected by district. The city operates under a Council/City Manager form of
government. It has experienced phenomenal growth, from 2.1 square miles with 26,000 residents in 1962
to 104.59 square miles and 167,000 residents today. This includes 482 acres of landscape green spaces in
the Landscape Assessment Districts and General Benefit Areas. Palmdale is ideally located in the high
desert of the Antelope Valley in Los Angeles County, 60 miles north of downtown Los Angeles. It is
bounded by the City of Lancaster to the north, Quartz Hill and Leona Valley to the west, Lake Los Angeles
and Littlerock to the east, and Acton to the south.

Palmdale has a desert landscape with a seasonal climate, open space, and plenty of room to breathe fresh
air. The people who live and work in Palmdale find a sense of place; the City has a young population with
residents looking to buy property, raise families, and work near home. Palmdale’s desert micro-climate
has freeze-and-thaw cycles during winter months and extreme heat during summer months. The City
encourages the incorporation of water-wise xeriscape landscaping in our LMD’s and general benefit areas.

biweekly service days and within the full span of each landscape service area. Failure to comply with this

Section L.

B.1  Service Frequency

at the following frequency, unless otherwise noted.

Landscape Assessment Districts
Services in all Landscape Assessment District locations shall be performed one time per week (weekly),

General Benefit Landscape Areas and Fairway Business Park

B.2  Drains and Grates
Drainage infrastructure including channels and gutters within maintained landscape areas and up to the
edge of asphalt pavement shall be kept free of vegetation, debris, and algae to allow the unrestricted flow
of water. Plugged drains, and missing or damaged grates shall be reported to the superintendent or
appointed designee immediately.

During regularly scheduled maintenance, the CONTRACTOR shall inspect all areas being serviced for the
presence of disease, insect and/or rodent infestation. The CONTRACTOR shall immediately notify the

SECTION G.  TREE MAINTENANCE SPECIFICATIONS

G.1  Minor Tree Maintenance Operations
The CONTRACTOR shall perform minor tree maintenance in each landscape service area (Landscape
Assessment Districts, General Benefit areas, and Fairway Business Park) including guying, staking, retying,
removal of tree stakes, juvenile tree pruning, and skirting of trees up to 7’. Tree pruning shall be in
accordance with ANSI 300 pruning standards. Trimming shall be performed for safety, overall aesthetic,
balance, health and to provide line of sight for traffic signs and pedestrian sidewalk clearance. City shall

G.2  Pruning
Most routine pruning to remove weak, diseased, or dead limbs can be accomplished at any time during
the year with little effect on the tree. As a rule, growth is maximized, and wound closure is fastest if pruning
takes place before the spring growth flush. Some trees, such as maples and birches, tend to “bleed” if
pruned early in the spring. It may be unsightly, but it is of little consequence to the tree.
  PAGE 19 of 45
  Request for Proposal No. 23-001-3610
 A few tree diseases, such as oak wilt, can be spread when pruning wounds allow spores access into the
tree. Susceptible trees should not be pruned during active transmission periods.

Heavy pruning just after the spring growth flush should be avoided. At that time, trees expended a great
deal of energy to produce foliage and early shoot growth. Removal of a substantial percentage of foliage
at this time can stress the tree. When to prune section contains consumer information provided by
International Society of Arboriculture.

G.3  Making Proper Pruning Cuts
Pruning cuts should be made just outside the branch collar. The branch collar contains trunk or parent
branch tissue and should not be damaged or removed. If the trunk collar has grown out on a dead limb to
be removed, make the cut just beyond the collar. Do not cut the collar.

If a large limb is to be removed, its weight should first be reduced. Making an undercut about 12 to 18
inches from the limb’s point of attachment accomplishes this. Make a second cut from the top, directly
above or a few inches farther out on the limb. Doing so removes the limb, leaving the 12- to 18-inch stub.
Remove the stub by cutting back to the branch collar. This technique reduces the possibility of tearing the
bark. Tree pruning shall be performed based on the following categories with the intent of developing
structurally sound trees symmetrical in appearance with the proper vertical and horizontal clearance. All
pruning and trimming operations shall be in accordance with ISA Standards.

  (a)  All suckers and sprouts shall be cut just outside the attachment collar to the trunk or limbs.
  (b)  All structural weaknesses such as a split crotch or limbs, or severe damage shall be
  reported to the superintendent or appointed designee.
  (c)  All trimmings and debris shall be removed and disposed of offsite at the end of each day’s
  work.
  (d)  Under no circumstances will stripping of lower branches be permitted in trees of 8” DBH
  or less. Lower branches shall be retained in a “tipped back” or pinched condition. Upon
  approval of the superintendent or appointed designee, skirting of lower branches may be
  done to mitigate irrigation coverage issues.

G.4  Staking and Tying
Trees, which shall be staked, fall into the following categories:
  (a)  Replacement of missing or damaged stakes where the tree diameter is less than six (6)
  inches.
  (b)  In those cases where a tree has been damaged and requires staking for support.
  (c)  For new trees or recently planted trees which have not previously been staked.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve Contract Services Agreement No. A-8702 with ROMTEC, Inc. for PN
  887, Marie Kerr Park Best of the West Concession Stand Project, in the amount
  of $239,557; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute Agreement No. A-8702
  with ROMTEC, Inc., including minimal and/or non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND

Project No. 887 involves purchasing and installing a concession stand building at the
Marie Kerr Park Best of the West Softball Complex. The 400-square-foot concession
building will offer snacks and beverages to park visitors and will be located north of the
existing restroom building, see Attachment 1.

This project is split into two phases:

Phase One entails purchasing and delivering a 400-square-foot prefabricated masonry
block building to the job site. The building footprint will include the necessary
appurtenances for the project and resemble the footprint included in Attachment 2.

Phase Two will include site preparation and installation of the building, and this phase will
be brought forward for Council approval in the future.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Award of PN 887, Agreement No. A-8702
March 6, 2024
Page 2

DISCUSSION

City staff evaluated various vendors through government pricing to provide a
prefabricated concession stand structure. ROMTEC, Inc. was identified as the best-
qualified vendor to design, produce, and deliver a concession stand structure.

ROMTEC, Inc. will provide stamped plans with calculations, including all architectural,
mechanical, structural, electrical, and plumbing plan sheets for review by the City’s
Planning and Building & Safety divisions. Upon City approval, ROMTEC, Inc. will deliver
the prefabricated structure to the project site.

The City is currently processing an agreement with a design consultant to prepare site
plans and specifications for the grading, drainage, foundation pad, and site utility
connections to support the prefabricated structure. The proposed project schedule is
described below:

   City Council Staff Report
DATE:  MARCH 6, 2024

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

FROM:  PUBLIC SAFETY DEPARTMENT

DISTRICT:  ALL

SUBJECT:  APPROVE THE SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE LEGAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH CIVICA LAW GROUP, APC, TO INCREASE THE
  AGREEMENT AMOUNT BY $420,000, FOR A TOTAL NOT TO
  EXCEED AMOUNT OF $1,020,000 FOR A CONTRACT TERM
  THROUGH MARCH 6, 2025.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the Second Amendment to the Legal Services Agreement No. A-8272
  with Civica Law Group, APC, to increase the agreement amount by $420,000, for
  a total not to exceed amount of $1,020,000 for a contract term through March 6,
  2025; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute the Second Amendment
  to Agreement No. A-8272 with Civic Law Group, APC, including minimal and/or
  non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

The City has previously contracted with Silver and Wright. In 2023, that firm dissolved,
and some of the attorneys formed the new firm of Civica Law Group, APC (Civica). The
attorneys from Civica continued their services to the City for specified legal services,
including code enforcement, public safety actions, and related litigation. Currently, the
budgeted contract amount has been depleted, primarily due to extended federal litigation,
and must now be augmented to allow them to provide services.

DISCUSSION

In March 2023, the City Council approved a contract between the City and Civica to
continue their code enforcement services for the City. This was concurrent with the
council engagement of Harper and Burns, LLC, for City Attorney services. It is noted that
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Second Amendment to Agrmt No. A-8272 with Civic Law Group, APC
March 6, 2024
Page 2

Harper and Burns can perform the same services as Civica, but allowing for continuity at
this time of transition, Civica will continue providing services until its contractual expiration
of March 6, 2025. At that time, the City will review the most efficient evaluation of such
legal services. In light of the ongoing federal litigation and code enforcement services, as
agreed upon in the 2023 contract, the City must now augment the contract amount for
Agreement No. A-8272 with Civica. It is expected that $420,000 will be sufficient for Civica
to continue its services until 2025.

RECOMMENDATION

Approve Agreement No. A-8696 with The Wellbeing Lab dba Louis Alloro, LLC, to
provide a Certificate in Applied Positive Psychology Program in an amount not to exceed
$275,000 for a term of one year.

Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Agreement No. A-8696 with The Wellbeing Lab dba Louis Alloro, LLC, to
  provide a Certificate In Applied Positive Psychology Program in an amount not to
  exceed $275,000 for a term of one year; and,

  2. Authorize the City Manager or her designee to execute the Agreement No. A-
  8696 with The Wellbeing Lab dba Louis Alloro, LLC, including minimal and/or
  non-substantial changes.

BACKGROUND

In 2021, in response to the community’s strong interest in making wellbeing resources
more widely available, the City offered the Wellbeing Lab Certificate in Applied Positive
Psychology Program (CAPP). The Program provides guidance and support in helping
teams thrive despite ongoing turbulence, uncertainty, disappointment, depression, or
worse. Research shows that wellbeing, the ability to feel good and function effectively,
helps us create workplaces, schools, organizations, and communities that are also
optimally functioning. The Program provides intelligent, evidence-based insights and
tools that deliver measurable results.

Below is a list of the second cohort’s impact projects:

SOWing Strength Seeds Workshop: a collaborative workshop to help unhoused youth
learn their character strengths and set goals;

Wellbeing for Families & Little Ones Curriculum: a curriculum program developed
for families and young people to explore wellbeing together;

PERMAH Cafe Workshop: an experience for Spanish speakers to come together and
learn PERMAH (Positive Emotion, Engagement, Relationships, Meaning,
Accomplishment, and Health);

REBUILD Workshop: a wellbeing workshop grounded in positive psychology to help
trauma survivors regain their strength and voice;

SHINE Workshop: a six-month experience for youth to meet regularly in different
locations around the Antelope Valley and increase their resilience and outlook using
science-based strategies;

Elevate: Connecting Hearts & Abilities Initiative: a workplace intervention designed
to help practitioners who work with developmentally disabled build their toolkit and
strategies; and,

Bank of PERMAH Workshop: a six-session workshop series designed to help seniors
with positive aging strategies grounded in positive psychology.

benefits of providing the community with a third cohort.

Procurement processes for expenditures using American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA)
funds generally follow state and local rules. In most cases, city procurement policies
will satisfy the federal requirements. One notable difference is that federal
procurement regulations mandate specific contract provisions in certain
circumstances. There are no requirements for contracts or expenditures of less than
$10,000. However, using ARPA funds for contracts in excess of $10,000 triggers the
mandatory contract provisions in 2 CFR Part 200, Appendix II.

Most contract provisions are required only on those exceeding $100,000 or those for
construction projects of any amount. However, mandatory contract provisions will
apply if a city obligates ARPA funds to a contract that exceeds $100,000.

For ease of administration, below is an explanation of the mandatory contract
provisions and model language necessary for compliance with federal law
disclosures.

2 C.F.R. PART 200: APPENDIX II, CONTRACT PROVISIONS

  • For contracts over $10,000, cities must include a provision that addresses
  termination for cause and convenience by the local government, including the
  process for termination and the basis for settlement.
  • For contracts over $100,000, cities must include a provision that addresses
  administrative, contractual, or legal remedies if a contractor violates or
  breaches the contract, including sanctions and penalties for the breach.
  • In accepting the ARPA award, local governments agreed to include an EEO
  statement in any federally assisted construction contract defined in 41 CFR
  Part 60-1.3. A federally assisted construction contract is defined as follows:
  o Any agreement or modification thereof between any applicant and a
  person for construction work which is paid for in whole or in part with
  funds obtained from the government or borrowed on the credit of the
  government pursuant to any federal program involving a grant, contract,
  loan, insurance, or guarantee, or undertaken pursuant to any federal
  program involving such grant, contract, loan, insurance, or guarantee,
  or any application or modification thereof approved by the government

   for a grant, contract, loan, insurance, or guarantee under which the
